text.content:
Three routes east. The harbor at sunset and the choice of which deck to stand on.

Once the party has named the broker, resolved Tamsin's fate, recovered what they can of the indictment package and understood the harbor-before-throne timing, they leave Hardby for Rel Astra. Rel Astra is fourteen hundred miles overland and two and a half thousand by sea, and the three routes are three answers to that. Say the weeks out loud before they choose.

The season. A Quiet Pursuit party leaves Hardby in early winter; a Commercial Cover party in midwinter; a delegation not until the back end of it. The packets run the mails in any weather short of one that sinks them. Traders are another matter — in deep winter Yorra Mel may simply not be sailing, and a party that wants the Lacquer Wave in Fireseek waits for her or takes the road. Say which season it is before they choose, because on the worst timing this page has two routes on it, not three.

The rule that shapes all three: the moment the party moves on the branch — the burglary, the subpoena, Vella's copies, any of it — Hardby sends word east. That dispatch goes by the fastest hull leaving the harbour. The only way to arrive before the report does is to be on that hull.

Route 1 — The Fast Packet (four and a half weeks)

The mail packets run Hardby to Rel Astra on a fixed schedule with a fresh crew at Saltmarsh, sailing through the night and stopping for nothing that is not the mails. Thirty days, near enough, in any weather that does not sink them.

What it costs

  • Money. Forty gold a head, and the master will want it all in advance and in Hardby coin. This is the price of a good horse each, for four and a half weeks of hard bunks.
  • Visibility. Total, and immediate. Packets carry the mails, so the passenger list is a document of record, read by the harbour authority at both ends. Cindren & Vhal Rel Astra will have the party's travelling names in hand before the gangplank is down.

What it buys

  • They beat the report. Hardby's dispatch about what the party did to the branch is on this packet or the next one. If the party is aboard, they arrive with the news rather than a fortnight behind it — and a PC who thinks to ask what else is in the mail bag is asking a very good question.
  • Four and a half weeks is short enough to still be angry in. Whatever Hardby cost them, they carry it into Rel Astra hot.
  • Arrival at the formal Customs Quay, not the Old Harbor. Correct, documented, and a long walk from the conspiracy's front door.

Phase 3 Pressure Clock: booking a packet berth is a matter of public record. If the clock stands at 3 or higher when they book, the firm knows which sailing they are on.

Route 2 — The Merchantman (seven weeks)

The Lacquer Wave, a Hardby-flagged wool trader working the long coast to Rel Astra's Old Harbor with stops at Saltmarsh and a half-dozen smaller ports, most of them unannounced. Forty-eight days, give or take the master's business. Her captain, Yorra Mel, is a Hardby woman with no firm ties and no questions, and she takes paying passengers at half the fare in advance.

What it costs

  • Seven weeks. The dispatch about the party reaches Rel Astra roughly eighteen days before they do. The firm will not be surprised; it will be ready.
  • Visibility. Partial. A trader files a cargo manifest, not a passenger list. Yorra Mel writes down bales. Anyone wanting the party's names would have to want them specifically, and ask her, and she would want to know why.
  • Cost. Eight gold a head, full fare, cabins shared.

What it buys

  • Seven weeks unreachable. No assassinations, no political pressure, no couriers from anyone, and nothing to do but read everything they recovered. This is the phase's decompression, and for a party that has just burgled a counting house it may be the most valuable thing on the page. Let them write letters. Let them argue.
  • Smuggling room. The hold is wool bales and salt cod. The evidence package folds into a bale and is forgotten; it will not be searched.
  • A Old Harbor arrival — the same district as Cindren & Vhal Rel Astra's main counting house. The party begins Phase 4 on the conspiracy's doorstep.

Phase 3 Pressure Clock: this route does not advance it at departure. Yorra Mel does not talk.

Route 3 — The Old Coastal Road (eight and a half weeks, or eleven behind a carriage)

East through Saltmarsh territory, around the southern end of the Wild Coast, and inland through the Aerdi southern provinces. Fourteen hundred and fifty miles of open, well-travelled, generally safe road, at the pace horses actually keep: sixty days, and closer to eighty if they are still riding behind the councilman.

What it costs

  • Two months, and every one of those days on Aerdi ground where the party has no standing. The first week out of Hardby is the dangerous one; after that they are ordinary road traffic. But the conspiracy has two months, and knows the road.
  • Interception scales with what Hardby knew. A party that left ahead of the firm's alarm rides clean. A party the firm had time to describe should expect a single hired blade somewhere in the third week, and a party that travelled as an accredited delegation should expect to be shadowed the entire way — with the escort itself as the deterrent.
  • Cost. Two gold a horse hired, three a remount; the party may already have mounts.

What it buys

  • No harbour authority anywhere in it. Direct entry to Rel Astra by the West Gate. No passenger list, no manifest, no clerk with a pen. This is the only route on which the party's arrival is not a document.
  • Optionality. The road passes within a day of the Whitemoor Estate and half a day of three other coastal estates the party may want to look at.

If they are still accredited — the councilman's carriage

A party that took the Official Delegation out of Loftwick and still holds its credentials can continue east in formal procession: the same councilman, the same clerks, the same escort, formal stops at every Aerdi customs post and an audience requested at the southern province governor's seat. Eleven and a half weeks, and the party does not control the schedule — the councilman does.

It buys three things nothing else on this page can:

  • Absolute legal protection. Full accreditation, pre-arranged audiences with the harbor commission and the Old Harbor Ward Council, immunity from arrest for the delegation's duration.
  • An audience with Tarlith Vhal Sereth. The delegation's standing means the party can request, and receive, a formal interview at his offices. This happens on no other route. Whether it yields anything is a Phase 4 question; the access is the value.
  • The Hardby warrant executes. Without diplomatic standing it is paper.

Phase 3 Pressure Clock: a formal procession cannot be hidden. +2 at departure. It matters less than it would on the other routes — the legal protection is itself the protection — but Phase 4 opens under maximum political weight.

Caelith's framing of the choice

By sealed letter (Letter 3; see Arrival → Caelith's Continuing Letters), Caelith has already given them his thinking. Paraphrased:

"If you are carrying the document that names him, send it to me by separate courier and travel with a copy. The original is safer in Trina's strongroom than in your saddlebags east of Hardby.

If you can afford the packet and can stomach being announced, take it — you will arrive with the letter about you rather than behind it, and I would rather they were surprised than prepared. If you cannot, take the trader; seven weeks at sea is seven weeks nobody can reach you, and you will need the rest more than you presently believe. Take the road only if you must arrive as nobody at all, and understand what two months on Aerdi ground costs.

And if you are still under the councilman's accreditation — stay under it. It is slow and it is loud and it will put you in a room with the man himself, and I do not know how to get you into that room any other way."

Loftwick had no clock; Loftwick had Caelith's house and a watcher on a corner. Hardby has a clock, and it runs fast. Hardby is a freer city, less restrained, and the conspiracy is operationally based here — they can act through hired hands and corrupt watchmen in ways they could not in Loftwick. Six segments, same shape as Phase 2's clock, but the threats are physical rather than political.

The clock at a glance — six escalating rhythms

  1. Recognition — someone in the city realizes who the party is.
  2. Surveillance — the firm puts watchers on the party's lodging.
  3. Witness loss — Vella, Hesren, Lerra, Veska, or Hella vanishes or is killed (GM picks based on which threads the party has activated).
  4. Hired blade — a single contracted attempt on a party member, not the whole group, in a public place.
  5. Squad attack — a coordinated mercenary assault on the party's lodging or on a single PC walking alone.
  6. The harbor closes — the firm pays the harbor watch to delay or seize ships and post-horses; the party's exit becomes a problem.

Triggers — what advances the clock

TriggerSegments
The party is recognized in Hardby (Quiet Pursuit only — see Arrival)+2
The party visits the Cindren & Vhal Hardby branch openly more than twice (Commercial Cover)+1
The Cindren & Vhal branch burglary succeeds+3 immediate
The Cindren & Vhal branch burglary is detected (Marsh wakes early, items missed)+1 additional
The party confronts Solen Mereth without a procedurally clean evidence package+2
The party confronts Tarsh in the Coopered Wreck and combat breaks out+1
The party kills Tarsh, Solen, or Mira Cindren+2 (firm assumes a third party in play; see Tarsh dossier)
Tamsin Moraven recovery raid (Black Cog Lane warehouse, Quiet Pursuit)+2
Tamsin Moraven recovery raid (Whitemoor Estate, Commercial Cover)+2
Subpoena filed against C&V Hardby (Official Delegation)+1
Each full session day in which the party makes no investigative progress in Hardby+1

Milestones — what happens at each segment

Segment 1 — Recognition

A face the party did not notice notices them. Could be a former C&V courier in a tavern, a watchman who was once on Reln Pollow's payroll back in Loftwick and has retired east, a Hardby waterfront fence who knew Sarth's name. The recognition is private and quiet; the recognizer reports to Solen Mereth or to Tarsh by morning. The firm now knows the party is in Hardby, even if they don't yet know what the party is doing.

Segment 2 — Surveillance

Two watchers are placed on the party's lodging — Castrian's house, the inn they took, the safe-house Ailen offered. The watchers are competent and uninteresting-looking; they note comings and goings and report to a runner three times daily. Perception DC 13 to spot one watcher; DC 16 to confirm the second. The party can make and break surveillance contact for game purposes (lose the watchers temporarily by going through Castrian's back garden, etc.) but the firm's intelligence picture sharpens with every additional day in the city.

Segment 3 — Witness loss

One of the party's contacts is taken or killed. GM picks based on which threads the party has activated and what would hurt most:

  • Vella Tannin — the sympathetic clerk. If the party has approached her and not yet extracted her, she vanishes between work and her lodging. Her body is found two days later in a barrel in the canal.
  • Hesren Vesh — if the party has approached him and not yet extracted him, he is "reassigned" to a coastal posting; the carriage taking him there does not arrive at its destination.
  • Lerra Voss — if the party recovered Tamsin's body or letter through her. She is taken on a quiet street.
  • Hella Voren — if Veska is gone and Hella is the party's primary contact. She is dismissed from the Quay clearing-house on a fabricated charge of misfiling.
  • Castrian Vell — if the party has nothing else to lose. His house is broken into; he is roughed up but not killed; he leaves Hardby for Saltmarsh within a week.

Segment 4 — Hired blade

A single contracted attempt on a single party member in a public place. A passing knife in a market crowd, a weighted purse swung at the back of the head outside a tavern, a single crossbow shot from a rooftop. The contractor is anonymous; if pursued, the trail goes cold within three streets. The attempt is meant to be survivable but to make the party's continuing presence in Hardby uncomfortable.

Segment 5 — Squad attack

A coordinated assault on the party's lodging or on a single PC walking alone. Four to six hired blades (six PCs: five to seven) (a Bandit Captain leading Bandits and Thugs), well-armed, professionally led. This is a real combat encounter and should be tuned for the party's level. The squad is not trying to kill all of the party — they are trying to recover specific items (the indictment package) and kill specific people (Tamsin, if she is with the party; the PC most likely to be carrying the documents). They will withdraw if the items are recovered or if they take more than 50% casualties.

Segment 6 — The harbor closes

The firm pays the harbor watch to delay shipping and post-horses. The Lacquer Wave's next sailing is "cancelled for repairs." The post-stable refuses to rent horses without seven days' written notice. Coastal galleys leave only with passenger lists pre-approved by the harbor commission, which is now slow-walking everything. The party's exit becomes a problem they must solve creatively — bribing a fishing skiff, hiring private mounts at triple price, calling on Castrian's wine-merchant friend to provide a private carriage, or simply leaving on foot.

Phase 4 begins under whatever exit conditions the party manages to engineer.

How to use the clock at the table

  • Show the players the clock face. Six segments, visible.
  • When you advance, say which trigger fired.
  • Phase 3's clock is faster than Phase 2's because Hardby is faster than Loftwick. Don't over-protect the party from segment 4 and 5 — these scenes are meant to happen, and they should land with appropriate stakes.
  • The clock should reach 4–5 segments by the time the party leaves Hardby. That is the intended outcome. Phase 4 begins with Cindren & Vhal Rel Astra fully aware that the Yeomanry hammer is on its way.

pages.name: Ending Read-Aloud — Departing for Rel Astra

text.content:
Read aloud at the moment the party leaves Hardby for Rel Astra. The text below is route-agnostic; adjust the small details (galley deck vs. road vs. carriage) to match the choice the party made.

Hardby in your last hour is the same as Hardby in your first: coal smoke and salt and the sound of a clock-tower bell that runs five seconds slow against every other clock you have heard since Loftwick. Whoever first set Hardby's main bell, three centuries ago, set it slightly wrong and no one has ever bothered to fix it. The city has run by it ever since.

You carry, in a pouch sewn into a wool bale or strapped under a saddle skirt or folded inside the lining of a diplomatic dispatch case, a copied indictment package —

[Quiet Pursuit, the branch burgled:] Veska Maelan's notarized opinion, three pages of carbon-copied second-set ledger entries (or, if you took the originals, the bound volumes themselves), Tarlith Vhal Sereth's signature impression rubbed up from the senior partner's blotter, and the chipped Hardby clearing-stamp that officially does not exist.

[Commercial Cover:] Veska Maelan's notarized opinion, Vella Tannin's carbon copies of the second set in her own careful hand, and Veska's sworn description of the chipped stamp and of the strongroom it sits in — which is, she says, worth more in a court than the stamp would be, because a thing hidden has to have been hidden by someone.

[Official Delegation:] Veska's notes, carried out of a shuttered office by a frightened young scribe; the notarized chop inventory the branch was obliged to let you read and not to take; and, in those notes, her sworn account of three documents she has seen in four years, all payouts to one private clearing account, all in the same small hand that is not Solen Mereth's.

The original of Veska's opinion is on its way back to Loftwick by separate courier; what you carry is your proof on the road.

You also carry — depending on what you accomplished — a living woman whose mother fed her wheat-water in the warehouse, or a small folded letter in her hand that you will need to put into her husband's hands when you next see him; an extracted clerk who has agreed to testify; a name (Anver Resh) who has agreed not to obstruct, in exchange for never appearing in your indictment.

You also carry, more quietly, what you have learned. The conspiracy is not Cindren and Vhal. The conspiracy is positioning to seat three commissioners on Rel Astra's harbor before the next Aerdy Overking is named, so that whoever wins the eastern succession finds Cindren-aligned hands controlling the eastern revenue. There are three vacant seats. There are three candidates. You do not yet know who the candidates are.

You do not yet know the name behind the single capital letter "E." You do not yet know whose hand wrote the only annotation Veska could not place. You do not yet know what is older than the conspiracy you have named.

Rel Astra rises out of the morning haze on the eastern shore — a month after Hardby if you bought the packet, two if you took a trader's hold or the coast road. The city is older than Hardby, larger than Loftwick, and runs on a clock that nobody set wrong: the harbor's, which keeps Aerdi imperial time exactly. Tarlith Vhal Sereth keeps an office on the Goldsmiths' Quarter side of the Old Harbor Ward, in a four-story building you have never seen and have, for two phases now, been preparing yourselves to walk into.

You have been travelling since Hardby for longer than you spent in it. Whatever you left unfinished there finished itself without you.

What the party leaves Phase 3 with

  • The names: Solen Mereth, Tarlith Vhal Sereth, Anver "Tarsh" Resh.
  • The indictment package — Veska's notarial opinion plus the recovered branch records (whether by burglary, copy-reading, or subpoena) plus the Sereth blotter rubbing plus the defect-stamp.
  • Tamsin's outcome resolved — alive (rescued from Hardby or Whitemoor) or dead (with body recovered and last letter in hand).
  • Hesren Vesh extracted or lost (depending on whether the party found him in time and on which travel approach made it possible).
  • The harbor-before-throne reading clarified. Three vacant seats on Rel Astra's harbor commission. Three candidates the conspiracy intends to seat before the next Overking is named. Identity of those candidates: unknown. Identity of the Aerdy claimant the conspiracy supports: unknown.
  • The fourth-hand "E." observation from Veska. Three small details about how the letter is formed. Phase 3 does not name Eclavdra. Phase 3 does not even know to look for her.

Where Phase 4 picks up

Phase 4 begins with the party's arrival in Rel Astra — the city the conspiracy actually operates from, the city where Tarlith Vhal Sereth keeps his offices, the city whose harbor commission is the conspiracy's prize. The Phase 4 questions are:

  • Who are the three candidate commissioners the conspiracy intends to seat?
  • Which Aerdy claimant do the conspirators support — or do they support none, intending instead to control the eastern revenue regardless of who wins?
  • Can Tarlith Vhal Sereth be brought to indictment in Aerdi court, or only in Yeomanry court via written deposition?
  • What is the older shape of the conspiracy that "E." sits behind?

Phase 4 may name "E." (it does not have to). Phase 4 may name the Aerdy claimant (it should). Phase 4 must, before its end, either bring Tarlith Vhal Sereth to court or remove him from play.

Phase 5, if there is one, is whatever is older than this.
